title: Universal scaling of spatially extended zero modes in inhomogeneous SSH chains
authors: Gilles Parez, Nicolas Crampé, Quentin Labriet, Lucia Morey, Luc Vinet
abstract: Protected zero modes are a hallmark of topological phases of matter and are exponentially localized at sharp interfaces between distinct gapped phases. We investigate how this picture changes for smooth interfaces in a broad class of inhomogeneous Su-Schrieffer-Heeger (SSH) models. Combining an exact lattice solution with an inhomogeneous Dirac description, we show that the associated Jackiw-Rebbi zero mode becomes spatially extended. For arbitrary smooth hopping profiles, its lattice extension universally scales as the square root of the system size, independently of the microscopic details of the interface. This emergent length defines a mesoscopic critical region separating two gapped phases, within which correlations decay algebraically before crossing over to exponential decay. In addition, the entanglement entropy scales as the logarithm of the emergent length near the interface, confirming the interpretation of a mesoscopic critical region. Our results establish a universal critical length governing the low-energy physics of smooth topological interfaces.
summary: This work analyzes the zero modes in inhomogeneous SSH chains where the transition between gapped phases occurs smoothly. The authors demonstrate that this smoothness causes the zero mode to spread out universally, scaling as $\sqrt{N}$. This emergent length scale dictates a mesoscopic critical region characterized by algebraic decay of correlations and logarithmic entanglement entropy growth.
main_problem: The study investigates how protected zero modes, characteristic of topological phases, behave when the interface between gapped regions is smooth rather than sharp.
main_result: For smooth interfaces in inhomogeneous SSH chains, the associated zero mode becomes spatially extended with a universal scaling length $\xi \sim \sqrt{N}$, defining a mesoscopic critical region. This leads to algebraic decay of correlations near the interface.
method: The analysis combines exact lattice solutions for the single-particle eigenproblem with continuum descriptions derived by promoting discrete hopping parameters to smooth functions, leading to an effective inhomogeneous Dirac Hamiltonian.
model_or_system: The system is based on the Su-Schrieffer-Heeger (SSH) model realized on a 1D bipartite lattice. The inhomogeneity is introduced via smoothly varying hopping amplitudes ($v_n, w_n$), which define the topological interface where the mass term $m(x)$ changes sign.
key_observables: Zero mode spatial extension ($\xi$), ground-state correlation function decay rate (algebraic vs. exponential), and entanglement entropy scaling near the interface.
important_parameters: System size ($N$), lattice spacing ($a$), and parameters defining the smoothness of the hopping profile (e.g., power-law or Fermi-Dirac profiles).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the existence of a well-defined continuum limit, requiring that the lattice couplings are invariant under rescaling to maintain smooth variation.
figures_summary:
Figures compare exact lattice results against continuum predictions for zero mode density and local topological markers ($
u_n$). They also show correlation functions collapsing onto universal scaling forms and entanglement entropy exhibiting logarithmic growth near the interface.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from defining the SSH Hamiltonian and solving the zero-energy eigenproblem on a discrete lattice. It then derives the continuum limit via scaling arguments, leading to an effective Dirac equation. Finally, it analyzes key observables like correlation functions and entanglement entropy using this continuous description.
why_interesting: The concept of an emergent mesoscopic critical region governed by universal length scales ($\xi \sim \sqrt{N}$) at a topological interface is highly relevant for understanding low-energy physics in engineered quantum materials or superconducting junctions.
